## file_impact widened: the merged commit touched a file the reviewed plan never declared

The close gate refused, correctly:

> cannot close: commit `ea08483d825e` changes `.github/workflows/gerrit-scanner-verify.yml`, which
> the recorded file_impact does not declare, so the work went beyond the reviewed plan.

The plan declared 5 paths; the commit touched **6**. The undeclared one is
`.github/workflows/gerrit-scanner-verify.yml` — a 4-line change (`4 ++--`), the scanner reusable's
Gerrit entry point, adjusted so the advisory job invoked from `gerrit-verify.yaml` resolves on a
patchset. Small, entirely in keeping with the ticket's intent, and exactly the kind of edit that
gets made without going back to update the plan.

That is what makes the check worth having. The point is not that this particular file was dangerous;
it is that "what was reviewed" and "what landed" had silently diverged, and nothing else in the
pipeline would have said so. A reviewer who approved a 5-file plan did not approve a 6-file change.

`file_impact` now declares all six with per-path reasons. I did **not** use `--force`, though the
error offers it: forcing here would close the ticket while leaving the plan permanently
misdescribing the work, which is the precise record-keeping failure this gate exists to prevent.

Widening file_impact is a material plan change, so it staled the plan-review attestation and a fresh
`rebar review-plan` is running before the close. For the record this is the **third** review pass on
this ticket, and each refusal was correct and for a different reason:

1. `[non-codebase]` AC ticked without the required `provenance:` continuation line — I had ticked the
   box on real evidence but never stated environment, principal, privilege posture and instrument.
2. Adding that provenance line was itself a material edit -> `stale-material`.
3. This one: undeclared file in the merged commit.

Worth noting the cost honestly, since it is not free: three LLM review passes to close one story.
That is the price of a plan whose declared scope has to match what landed, and on this evidence the
gate is earning it — none of the three was spurious. The avoidable part was mine: had I declared the
file impact from the merged commit and written the provenance line in the same edit as the tick, one
pass would have done.
